rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: Let \(a = p^2 q^3 r^n\) and \(b = p^3 q^m r^2\), where p, q, r are prime numbers. If LCM of a and b is \(p^3 q^4 r^3\), then the value of \(3n - 2m\) is
rows.solution:
The LCM takes the highest power of each prime.

For q: the higher of \(q^3\) and \(q^m\) is \(q^4\), so \(m = 4\). For r: the higher of \(r^n\) and \(r^2\) is \(r^3\), so \(n = 3\).

\(3n - 2m = 9 - 8 = 1\), which is option (B) \(1\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem:
The point P divides the line segment AB in the ratio 3 : 1 as shown below :

The value of \(\dfrac{AB}{PB}\) is
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the segment AB with P marked between A and B, nearer B; the stem states that P divides AB in the ratio 3 : 1. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
P divides AB in the ratio \(3 : 1\), so AB is 4 parts and PB is 1 part.

\(\dfrac{AB}{PB} = \dfrac{4}{1} = 4\), which is option (C) \(4\).

rows.stem: Which of the following equations is a quadratic equation ?
rows.solution:
Expand each and see what degree is left:

\(x^3 = (x - 1)^3 + 3x^2 = x^3 - 3x^2 + 3x - 1 + 3x^2\) gives \(3x - 1 = 0\), which is linear.

\(x^3 = (x + 1)^3 = x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 1\) gives \(3x^2 + 3x + 1 = 0\), which is quadratic.

\(x^2 = \sqrt{x}\) contains \(\sqrt{x}\), so it is not a polynomial equation.

\(x^2 + 1 = \dfrac{1}{x}\) gives \(x^3 + x - 1 = 0\) on multiplying by x, which is cubic.

This is option (B) \(x^3 = (x + 1)^3\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: A piggy bank contains ₹ 1 coins and ₹ 2 coins in the ratio 9 : 11 respectively. The piggy bank is accidently dropped and a coin pops out of it. The probability that it is a ₹ 2 coin is
rows.solution:
The coins are in the ratio \(9 : 11\), so 11 of every 20 coins are ₹ 2 coins.

\(P(\text{two-rupee coin}) =\dfrac{11}{20} = 0.55\), which is option (C) \(0.55\).

rows.stem: The value of \(\dfrac{2 \tan 60^\circ}{1 - \tan^2 60^\circ}\) is same as the value of

**Assertion (A) :** For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\sec\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \tan\theta = 2\sqrt{2}\).

**Reason (R) :** \(\sec^2\theta = 1 - \tan^2\theta\) for all values of \(\theta\).
rows.context: Directions : In Question Numbers 19 and 20, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option from following :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
For an acute angle \(\tan\theta > 0\), and \(\tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta - 1 = 9 - 1 = 8\), so \(\tan\theta = 2\sqrt{2}\). The Assertion is true.

The identity is \(\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta\), not \(1 - \tan^2\theta\) (at \(\theta = 45^\circ\), \(\sec^2\theta = 2\) while \(1 - \tan^2\theta = 0\)). The Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem: AD and PS are angle bisectors of \(\angle A\) and \(\angle P\) of triangles ABC and PQR. If \(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta PQR\), prove that \(\Delta ACD \sim \Delta PRS\).
rows.solution:
\(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta PQR\), so \(\angle BAC = \angle QPR\) and \(\angle C = \angle R\).

AD and PS bisect \(\angle A\) and \(\angle P\), so \(\angle CAD = \dfrac{1}{2}\angle BAC = \dfrac{1}{2}\angle QPR = \angle RPS\).

In triangles ACD and PRS, \(\angle CAD = \angle RPS\) and \(\angle C = \angle R\), so \(\Delta ACD \sim \Delta PRS\) (AA similarity).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem:
All the face cards are removed from the pack of 52 cards and a card is drawn at random from the remaining cards. Find the probability that the card so drawn is

(i) a spade.

(ii) not an ace.
rows.solution:
Removing the 12 face cards leaves \(52 - 12 = 40\) cards, 10 of each suit.

(i) There are 10 spades, so \(P(\text{a spade}) = \dfrac{10}{40} = \dfrac{1}{4}\).

(ii) All 4 aces remain, so \(P(\text{not an ace}) = \dfrac{40 - 4}{40} = \dfrac{36}{40} = \dfrac{9}{10}\).

rows.subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
rows.stem: Obtain the zeroes of the polynomial \(p(x) = 2x^2 - 5x - 3\). Hence, obtain a polynomial each of whose zeroes is one less than each of the zero of \(p(x)\).
rows.solution:
\(2x^2 - 5x - 3 = 2x^2 - 6x + x - 3 = 2x(x - 3) + 1(x - 3) = (x - 3)(2x + 1)\).

The zeroes are \(3\) and \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\).

One less than each zero: \(2\) and \(-\dfrac{3}{2}\).

Sum \(= 2 - \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\); product \(= 2 \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = -3\).

The polynomial is \(x^2 - \dfrac{1}{2}x - 3\), or \(2x^2 - x - 6\) (any non-zero multiple of it).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem:
Solve the following system of equations graphically :

\(2x + y = 5\) and \(4x - y = 7\). Hence, write the coordinates of the points where given lines meet y-axis.
rows.solution:
Points on \(2x + y = 5\) (that is, \(y = 5 - 2x\)):

| \(x\) | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 5 | 3 | 1 |

Points on \(4x - y = 7\) (that is, \(y = 4x - 7\)):

| \(x\) | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | \(-7\) | \(-3\) | 1 |

Plot both sets of points and draw the two lines. They meet at \((2, 1)\), so the solution is \(x = 2\), \(y = 1\).

The lines meet the y-axis at \((0, 5)\) and \((0, -7)\).

rows.stem:
During a medical checkup, height of 35 students of a class were recorded as follows :

| **Height (in cm)** | 90-100 | 100-110 | 110-120 | 120-130 | 130-140 | 140-150 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Number of Students** | 3 | 2 | 4 | 5 | 14 | 7 |

Find the difference between the mean height and median height.

State the converse of basic proportionality theorem.

Also find \(\dfrac{BF}{FC}\) in the following figure, given that \(AB \parallel DC \parallel EF\) and \(\dfrac{AE}{ED} = \dfrac{2}{3}\).

Also, find the length of EF if AB = 10 cm and DC = 15 cm.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the drawing alone places E on AD and F on BC of the trapezium ABCD (AB the upper base, DC the lower, arrows marking AB, EF and DC parallel) and shows the dashed diagonal AC cutting EF at G, the construction the scheme's working uses. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
Converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem: if a line divides any two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then the line is parallel to the third side.

Let the diagonal AC cut EF at G.

In triangle ADC, \(EG \parallel DC\), so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem \(\dfrac{AG}{GC} = \dfrac{AE}{ED} = \dfrac{2}{3}\).

In triangle CAB, \(GF \parallel AB\), so \(\dfrac{BF}{FC} = \dfrac{AG}{GC} = \dfrac{2}{3}\).

For EF: \(AE : ED = 2 : 3\) gives \(\dfrac{AE}{AD} = \dfrac{2}{5}\). Since \(EG \parallel DC\), \(\Delta AEG \sim \Delta ADC\), so \(\dfrac{EG}{DC} = \dfrac{AE}{AD} = \dfrac{2}{5}\) and \(EG = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 15 = 6\) cm.

Similarly \(\dfrac{CG}{CA} = \dfrac{3}{5}\), and \(\Delta CGF \sim \Delta CAB\), so \(\dfrac{GF}{AB} = \dfrac{3}{5}\) and \(GF = \dfrac{3}{5} \times 10 = 6\) cm.

\(EF = EG + GF = 6 + 6 = 12\) cm.
